description: Every ERROR and WARN entry that a complete runGameTestServer log is expected to contain. Each expectation records a deliberate refusal or failure path that a named GameTest drives, or a bounded environment warning. scripts/check_gametest_log.py fails on any FATAL entry, any entry not listed here and any count that differs.

expectations.message: Exception caught during firing event: W37F injected respawn listener interruption
expectations.reason: A HIGHEST respawn listener throws after native replacement insertion; the test catches the deliberate exception and verifies the persisted tuple is restored on a later tick.

expectations.message: Exception caught during firing event: W37F injected respawn listener interruption
expectations.reason: W37I: each test enters W37F's interrupted-listener window with the same deliberate HIGHEST respawn listener exception, catches it, and checks the old connection player's logout save and the reconnect.

expectations.message: Force-added player with duplicate UUID [0-9a-f-]{36}
expectations.reason: W37I: after the old connection player's logout save, vanilla leaves the unadopted replacement in its Level, so each test's reconnect force-adds the new player and discards the replacement, as vanilla does for a real reconnect after that window.

expectations.message: ARCE_PLANET_RESPAWN_DIAGNOSTIC player=[0-9a-f-]{36} case=unencodable_tuple: the saved respawn tuple is outside the backup bounds, so its refusal is skipped and vanilla reads it; recovery: set a valid respawn point, for example with /spawnpoint \(ADR-066 planet respawn backup note\)
expectations.reason: W37H F5: one dead player gets a NaN angle and then an out-of-bounds x on later ticks; the skipped refusal is reported once per player per server session.

expectations.message: ARCE_PLANET_RESPAWN_DIAGNOSTIC player=[0-9a-f-]{36} case=unreadable_backup: ForgeData\.PlayerPersisted\.arce_planet_respawn_backup is unreadable or from a later version and is kept verbatim, so the player respawns without it; recovery: with the player offline, back up the player file and copy its tuple to the Spawn fields \(ADR-066 planet respawn backup note\)
expectations.reason: W37H F5: the same player carries a schema 99 backup root, which is kept verbatim and reported once per player per server session.

expectations.message: ARCE_PLANET_RESPAWN_DIAGNOSTIC player=[0-9a-f-]{36} case=foreign_persisted_parent: ForgeData\.PlayerPersisted is not a compound, so a refused point cannot be set aside and vanilla reads it; recovery: with the player offline, back up the player file and make ForgeData\.PlayerPersisted a compound \(ADR-066 planet respawn backup note\)
expectations.reason: W37H F5: a dead player has a string PlayerPersisted parent; it is not overwritten, and the skipped refusal is reported once per player per server session.

expectations.message: ARCE_STATION_WARP_ENERGY_DROPPED station=[0-9a-f-]{36} energy=\d+
expectations.test: StationWarpGameTests, StationWarpAbortGameTests, TauCetiPathGameTests, StationControlsGameTests, StationControllerMenuGameTests, StationNoticeGameTests
expectations.reason: Each test ends or aborts a charged warp, and the station must record the warp energy it drops. StationControlsGameTests deletes one charged station after a quote (core reach), one after its cancelled confirmations (confirm core) and two after their warps (parity). StationControllerMenuGameTests deletes four charged stations after their refused or cancelled confirmations (confirm binding). StationNoticeGameTests deletes one charged station after its warp in each of the delivery, login and notice-failure tests.

expectations.test: environment: vanilla generation of a newly loaded chunk
expectations.reason: Vanilla world generation (WorldGenRegion.setBlock, offsets 154-164 in Forge 47.4.10) stores a DUMMY block-entity tag when it places a block-entity block in a generating chunk; a later generation step can replace that block with air without removing the tag. LevelChunk logs this pair when the new chunk is loaded. ARCE code never writes DUMMY. Whether a test layout reaches such a chunk depends on batch positions, so it is admitted in any batch, for air only, at most four times. First seen in hosted run 38498876649 (batch force_field, chunk 3,21).
